## Failure paths and arms (fill in)

The machine chain above covers the legacy/canonical/v2 fixtures plus the two-user lifecycle baseline. The additional retirement arms use the **same frozen candidate** and real FreeIPA/SSSD/OpenSSH services on the same three disposable targets. [Native lifecycle summary](issue-226-native.json) records all six checkpoint assertions, 88 command exit codes/log hashes, driver/binary/controller fingerprints and unchanged archive source closure. Full stdout/stderr and journal/LDAP observations remain in the referenced external artifact directory; they are not appended here.

| Arm | Actual result |
|---|---|
| Initial effective keys | Both users have exact key A on both clients; four fresh public-key-only SSH logins succeed; no pending work. |
| Optional/offline client | Actual reconcile returns rc 1 / SSH PARTIAL; exactly two user/retired-alias pairs remain. Live client has exact B, accepts B and rejects A. The suspended VM is resumed. |
| Early scope guards | Omitted inventory and cross-stage applies each return rc 2 at the intended guard. Journal bytes, native user attributes/keys, host/DNS state remain unchanged; the requested sentinel group is absent. |
| Direct roster absent | Native host and owned DNS A cleanup precede a separate retired receipt with discharged=2, including the omitted user. No retired SSH or legacy refresh occurs. Omitted desired/native state is preserved; repeated apply is changed=0 with the same receipt. |
| Inventory already removed | Without mapping, rc 2 leaves journal bytes unchanged. Exact operator alias/FQDN/stage/reason/origin mapping permits only the selected retirement; live B allow/A deny and omitted-user preservation hold. |
| Formal decommission interruption | The watcher observes host present then authoritative LDAP rc 32 before making only the journal immutable. Actual apply returns rc 1 / EPERM after host/owned-A deletion; both pending pairs and inventory remain, with no receipt. The watcher and immutable flag are removed. The original plan resumes to completed, client unenrolls, and inventory is removed last. Repeated resume returns already_completed with a stable journal. A subsequent real reconcile produces exact live C, C allow/B deny, preserved omitted-user state and zero retired pending pairs. |

One **controller transport incident** is retained separately in the native summary: checkpoint 5 attempt 1 used a stale task-owned SSH multiplex connection after VM rollback. Non-multiplexed native SSH succeeded; only verified task processes were terminated. Its rc 2 was controller-aborted before the pending guard and receives no acceptance credit. Journal bytes and native IPA state were unchanged. Task-only control masters were closed, and the identical checkpoint was rerun from the same pending-B snapshot; the intended no-mapping guard then rejected in 4.227 seconds and authorized recovery passed. The original failed logs/manifests, reset receipts and retry linkage remain available.

Persistent file/directory fsync EIO is separately tested through the original Python helper and real Ansible/provider Inspect/Verify with a syscall fault shim. First retire, identical retry and settled-status proof all fail while EIO persists; after clearing it, all three success outlets confirm file+directory barriers without changing receipt/journal bytes. The 23 helper tests, targeted Go/Ansible regressions and nine discriminating negative controls pass on this candidate. These harness failures are not claimed as native VM crashes.

Earlier candidates and the controller tmpfs-inode failure are superseded history, not this candidate's passing result. Required source fixes were frozen before this run. Task-only topology teardown passed after capture: all three i226 targets and their image directories are absent; all four unrelated domains present immediately before teardown remain.
